messages.text:
"I want to build a 2D top-down arena battle game inspired by \"Footmen Frenzy\" using HTML5, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript (rendered on an HTML Canvas). 

1. A square canvas arena with 4 player bases (one in each corner: Top-Left, Top-Right, Bottom-Left, Bottom-Right).
2. A game loop running at 60 FPS handling updating and drawing.
3. A basic \"Spawner\" class for each base that automatically spawns a weak melee unit (a \"Footman\") every 5 seconds.
4. A \"Unit\" class for these footmen. Units should automatically move toward the dead center of the map to fight any unit from an opposing team.
5. Simple collision and melee combat logic (if opposing units touch, they deal damage to each other until one dies).

1. A \"Hero\" class for each team. The Hero is a larger, stronger unit with higher HP and damage.
2. Team 1 (Top-Left) is the player. Allow the player to right-click on the canvas to move their Hero to that position (pathfinding can be straight-line for now).
3. If the player right-clicks an enemy unit, the Hero should pursue and attack it.
4. The other 3 teams are AI-controlled. Their Heroes should automatically roam near the center, attacking nearby enemies.
5. When any unit or Hero kills an enemy, the owning player gets 10 Gold. Display the player's Gold count in a simple HTML overlay on the top of the canvas.

Let's add the upgrade economy. Add a UI overlay side-panel next to the canvas with three buttons that cost Gold:
1. \"Upgrade Spawn Speed\" (Costs 50 gold): Reduces the base's unit spawn timer by 0.5 seconds.
2. \"Upgrade Unit Tier\" (Costs 100 gold): Changes the base's spawns from \"Tier 1 Footmen\" (low stats) to \"Tier 2 Knights\" (higher HP/damage, different color).
3. \"Revive Hero\" (Costs 150 gold, only clickable if Hero is dead): Spawns the player's Hero back at their base corner after a 10-second delay.

Ensure the enemy AI teams automatically buy these upgrades whenever they happen to hoard enough gold. (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
